It's a bit beside the point, but we should also mention that, at least based on early screenshots, EA's message includes a typo, writing "awating signal" instead of "awaiting signal." title: Xbox at 25: My Memories From Across Xbox’s Entire (and Quite Incredible) History
snippet: The first day of my career was October 1, 2002. I’d been lucky enough to get hired by Official Xbox Magazine. The fledgling Xbox console was not quite a year ol...
fullText: The first day of my career was October 1, 2002. I’d been lucky enough to get hired by Official Xbox Magazine. The fledgling Xbox console was not quite a year old, and when I got settled in on the staff, it quickly became clear that Xbox was really about one thing above all else: Halo. I remember being surprised in my first days on the job by what would happen every single day, like clockwork, at 5pm: consoles and TVs would get turned on, Halo would get fired up, and we’d all play a round or two of Capture the Flag on Blood Gulch before we all went home. Fun and friendly banter ensued. Halo was baked into the Xbox’s DNA from the very start.It is one of my very first of many thousands of great Xbox memories. I’ve been lucky enough to have a front-row seat for most of the Xbox’s 25 years, covering the high highs and low lows of Microsoft’s pivot into the living room. It’s been quite a ride since November 15, 2001, and I wanted to mark the occasion by sharing some of my biggest memories with you. And, like everything else with Xbox, it started with Halo.Thank goodness for Combat Evolved, in fact, because most of the rest of that first year of Xbox history was pretty bleak. Lots of C++ spaghetti was thrown at the wall, and most of it didn’t stick. Oh, don’t get me wrong – there were moments! Steel Battalion, Capcom’s batshit-insane mech vertical tank simulator that cost $200 and came with its own custom 40-button controller and foot pedals was quite simply amazing as both a game and piece of hardware and would never get made today. Meanwhile, The Elder Scrolls 3: Morrowind was the beginning of Xbox becoming a Western-RPG powerhouse. But first-party hadn’t really found its footing yet, as it published stuff like the now-infamous Blinx: The Time Sweeper.But thanks to Combat Evolved carrying the Xbox through its first trip around the sun, things got really interesting in Year Two. It turns out I joined the magazine at just the right time! Halo: Combat Evolved was the biggest very real reason to buy the console in its first year, but its critical second year was defined by three things: Xbox Live, Tom Clancy games, and BioWare. Year TwoXbox Live was a massive swing that connected for a home run. Back then, high-speed internet was far from ubiquitous. In fact, dial-up 56k modems still dominated the American online infrastructure. But Microsoft put a big bet on broadband by putting an Ethernet port into every Xbox. In the first year, that port only got used for Halo LAN (er, System Link) parties, but then, on the one-year anniversary of the system on November 15, 2002, Xbox Live launched. And it was a loud launch in the very best of ways. MechAssault brought an action-first take on MechWarrior to the console audience – including an excellent multiplayer suite – while a faithful port of the PC’s outstanding military FPS Tom Clancy’s Ghost Recon was a perfect fit for the new online service. title: League of Legends: New Dawn Unveiled With Debut Trailer, Riot Announces Major Overhaul Coming in 2027

fullText: At the 2026 League of Legends World Championship Finals, Riot Games officially unveiled League of Legends: New Dawn. The large-scale update is scheduled for 2027 and will bring changes to the game's client, Summoner's Rift, visuals, and gameplay, marking the beginning of a new chapter for one of the industry's most enduring titles.New Dawn introduces what Riot described as an "all-encompassing" update to League, touching almost every aspect of its experience. "This is the start of a new era for League, a new journey," said Paul Bellezza, League's executive producer, in New Dawn's first official trailer. Riot is expected to share the full reveal of New Dawn this coming January.A new look for Summoner's RiftThe announcement came with a trailer shown at Worlds Finals that offered the first glimpse of what League players can expect from New Dawn, and the changes appear to go beyond simple refreshed graphics. The first noticeable change is a redesigned champion selection screen, which looks much closer to the modern interface found in Wild Rift, League's mobile game. The footage also hints at a new or reworked rune system, which seems to have a much bigger impact on the gameplay than ever before. The trailer also showcased updated minions, a new look for Summoner's Rift, redesigned dragons and Baron Nashor, as well as what seem to be new visual effects for many champion abilities. More interestingly, the footage also hinted at gameplay changes that will change how players approach their matches, including major changes to the map terrain that open new strategic consideration — and not only for junglers. Since its launch in 2009, League has seen more than a few major changes, including a rebuilt Summoner's Rift in 2014, a new client a couple of years later, and runes and then terrain changes in the following years. Still, nothing ever came close to the scale of what New Dawn promises to be. For now, Riot is keeping the full extent of these gameplay changes to itself, leaving much of New Dawn's scope to be revealed in the coming months. Leaving the past behindRiot spent part of 2026 looking back at League's history through League Classic, a mode that allowed players to revisit older versions of both the Summoner's Rift and League's champions. However, nostalgia alone proved difficult to sustain. Just a few weeks after its release, Riot announced that the mode would end its current run in January 2027. The experience could return in a modified format in the future, but it demonstrated that revisiting the past is not necessarily enough to keep a game of League's scale moving forward.Now, Riot is looking in the opposite direction. 18 years since League first launched, New Dawn represents another attempt at evolving a game whose identity has been shaped as much by its community as by its developers. title: GTA 6 Will Do Something the Franchise Has Never Done Before: Encourage Empathy

fullText: Rockstar has confirmed GTA 6 features something the franchise has never had before: mechanisms that encourage empathy.Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson and head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe talked about how next week's Grand Theft Auto changes the formula the series is known for during an interview with The Guardian (via @GameRoll_). Jason and Lucia will surely be able to cause a fair amount of chaos when players take control in Vice City, but in a post-Red Dead Redemption 2 world, they'll have the freedom to be kind, too."Crime is a fundamental part of GTA – at least up until now, it has been," Nelson said. "We're trying to make sure we're not punishing people for playing the game they are used to … [but] your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out."Games like GTA 5 have given players playgrounds and characters that can maximize the mayhem. Trevor, one of that game's three protagonists, is a great example of this chaotic energy, but in GTA 6, there doesn't seem to be a direct equivalent. Sure, Rockstar's trademark tone and instantly recognizable characters can be seen all over what few trailers we've received thus far, but everything seems a bit more grounded, too.Falling in line with this is the news that GTA 6 will feature a world that might actually reward those who take the citizens of Leonida into consideration. Of course, that doesn't mean those who prefer to wreak havoc won't be able to play their way, too. It just means that, at least based on Nelson's words, there's some room to be a normal or even good person, too."I would say so," he replied when asked if the new game would encourage empathy in some capacity. "I would say that it's a product of the story we're trying to tell. We've tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to."Elsewhere in the interview, Nelson described Jason and Lucia as a "younger couple with their backs against the wall," which is why it doesn't make sense for them to "go out and cause as much carnage and make as much noise as they can." This isn't Michael, Franklin, or Trevor, nor is it Niko Bellic. Thankfully, we won't have to wait too much longer to find out just what kind of criminals Jason and Lucia are, or who they can be.GTA 6 launches November 19, 2026, for PS5 and Xbox Series X | S. With more grounded in-game mechanisms and NPCs that react to weapons, it's clear we're staring down what will likely be the most realistic Grand Theft Auto game so far. It's something that has plenty of fans excited and others nervous. Recent footage shared by Rockstar has highlighted the game's unbelievable graphics. It's something that has IGN writer Jacqueline Thomas excited, even if it does run at 30 fps.

title: PS5 QSSR Updates Revealed for Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Arc Raiders, and More
snippet: Sony has confirmed Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Arc Raiders, and four more games are receiving QSSR support on base PS5s.The list of six newcomers joining the sma...
fullText: Sony has confirmed Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Arc Raiders, and four more games are receiving QSSR support on base PS5s.The list of six newcomers joining the small-but-growing group of supported games was unveiled in a PlayStation.Blog post. In addition to confirmation that incoming updates will add QSSR (Quick Spectral Super Resolution), the post included testimonials from each of the studios' developers, who shared how the tech will impact visuals.When Sony pulled back the curtain on QSSR in October, it came with confirmation that it had already been implemented in Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yōtei. Now, we know that Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Remedy Entertainment's Control Resonant, Embark Studios' Arc Raiders and The Finals, Hello Games' No Man's Sky, and Expression Games' Hell Let Loose: Vietnam will soon take advantage of the AI upscaling tech.In the case of Marvel's Spider-Man 2, QSSR is available as part of a new update that's out now."Having seen great results integrating QSSR in Marvel’s Wolverine, our team decided to bring it to Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 as well, in an update that’s live now!" Insomniac head of technology Mike Fitzgerald said. "We’re excited for players to swing back into our 2023 title and see QSSR’s exciting image stability and sharpness benefits in both Fidelity and Performance modes."Remedy said QSSR will bring noticeable improvements in image stability and fine detail when it launches in a new update in December. Hello Games founder Sean Murray, meanwhile, promised that players can look forward to No Man's Sky looking "sharper, cleaner, and more beautiful" at the "best possible framerate" in the next few weeks. When exactly The Finals, Arc Raiders, and Hell Let Loose: Vietnam will receive their updates has yet to be announced."With the new QSSR coming soon to ARC Raiders and The Finals, we can deliver increased sharpness, better environmental clarity, and overall visual improvements to even more PlayStation players," Embark said. "We are very happy to see Sony’s continued investment in PlayStation technology translate into meaningful improvements for all players, bringing more immersive experiences across the PlayStation ecosystem."Sony then teased that developers interested in using QSSR are "just getting started." More PS5 games are set to receive similar updates in the coming months, though which titles will join the list remains to be seen.

title: Rainbow Six: Vegas Reportedly Returning With New Installment
snippet: Ubisoft has reportedly given a new entry in the Rainbow Six: Vegas series the green light and a codename.Details on a long-awaited (and unexpected) return to a ...
fullText: Ubisoft has reportedly given a new entry in the Rainbow Six: Vegas series the green light and a codename.Details on a long-awaited (and unexpected) return to a fan-favorite corner of the Rainbow Six universe come from an Insider Gaming report. The publisher is said to have given its Ubisoft Montreal team the go-ahead to begin work on a new Vegas installment, with two other projects reportedly also in the works there.Rainbow Six: Vegas started with the release of the original game in 2006 before it returned for a sequel in 2008. Whether the new game will be called Rainbow Six: Vegas 3 or something else is unclear, though the site's sources say it's expected to be more like the former rather than something like a remake. It also stated that it's being worked on with the apt codename, "Spades."That's just one of the three games the Montreal studio is reportedly working on. The report wasn't able to confirm much about the remaining projects but said one source suggested at least one other game is planned to take place in the Rainbow Six universe in some capacity.The Rainbow Six franchise as a whole existed long before popular entries like Rainbow Six Siege or even the Vegas series. Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six traces all the way back to the late '90s but has splintered into a wide variety of gameplay experiences and offerings. Siege is no doubt the most well-known iteration today thanks to how Ubisoft has supported its tactical gameplay since its 2015 launch, but the most recent entry actually arrived in 2022 with Rainbow Six Extraction.Despite nearly 20 years passing since the last Vegas game, it's remained a beloved corner of the universe for many. IGN gave the original game a 7.6/10 when it launched for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. We then gave the sequel's limited edition release an 8.4/10.Ubisoft seems to be still in the early stages of its unannounced Rainbow Six: Vegas continuation, so don't expect to see it launch for at least a few more years. While that may mean we'll have passed the 20-year mark since the last game, we hopefully won't have to wait quite as long to learn more about it. Until then, it's best to keep expectations low while the publisher keeps its cards close to its chest.Meanwhile, we do know about a few other projects Ubisoft has up its sleeve. Rainbow Six Tactics, for example, was announced in August and will launch sometime next year. A Splinter Cell remake is also in the works, even if it's been a while since we heard from it.

title: This Legend of Zelda Triforce Brain Teaser Is Only $13 for Black Friday
snippet: Update 11/14: The Triforce puzzle sold out, but the Master Sword puzzle is now on sale for $12.88. It's rated a level 6 (out of 6) difficulty, and aimed at ...
fullText: Update 11/14: The Triforce puzzle sold out, but the Master Sword puzzle is now on sale for $12.88. It's rated a level 6 (out of 6) difficulty, and aimed at ages 12+. The Legend of Zelda games are filled with puzzles for Link to solve. Now there’s a Zelda-themed puzzle for you to solve outside of the games, in real life. It’s a cast metal Triforce, like you’d find in most Zelda games, but it’s a brain teaser. The goal is to figure out how to take it apart, and then figure out how to put it back together. It’s on sale now on Amazon for $12.88, a new all-time low price. Legend of Zelda Triforce Hanayama Metal Brain Teaser Is 60% OffThe puzzle is made by Hanayama, a Japanese company that specializes in these kinds of brain-teasers. The company actually makes five different Zelda-themed puzzles, but none of the others happen to be on sale at the moment. Hanayama makes a bunch of other non-Zelda-themed puzzles as well, so you can check them out if you like this one.This Triforce puzzle is comprised of four interlocking metal pieces. Your job is simply to figure out how to slide the pieces around to take them apart. Then, once you have the puzzle disassembled, you can try to re-assemble it.Hanayama puzzles – or Huzzles, as they're sometimes called – are rated in terms of difficulty, with level 1 being the easiest and level 6 being the hardest. This Triforce puzzle rings in at level 5, so it ought to be pretty tough to figure out. It's aimed at puzzle solvers age 12 and up.This puzzle, and the other Zelda puzzles that have gone on sale previously, have been incredibly popular with the IGN audience. According to Amazon price tracker Camelcamelcamel, this is the lowest price this puzzle has ever been, and it's by far the cheapest it's been in over a year. It’s unclear when the sale will end, so grab it before the price goes back up.I’m all about that Hyrule life lately, as I've been playing the Switch 2 Ocarina of Time remake and loving every second of it. I’ll probably pick one of these up as a stocking stuffer for the kids.

fullText: Wizards of the Coast is hosting a preview panel at MagicCon Atlanta, showing off all the sets coming to Magic in 2027. While we know of most of the in-universe sets coming to the game next year, the real mystery is the two yet-to-be revealed Universes Beyond crossover sets. Unfortunately, WotC didn't spend any time showing off the next Universes Beyond sets, and just focused on Nauctis: The Sunken Realm, the first set that will be coming out February 5, 2027. Preorders are now up on Amazon for the new set, and there was a fun little segment with puppets and Brian Henson, so that helped a little bit.
